newsitem.title: MEXICO: New Mexico attorney gen'l vows progress on Colosio.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico attorney gen'l vows progress on Colosio.

text.p: In his first day on the job, Mexico's new attorney general on Tuesday promised to "untangle" the complicated investigation into the 1994 assassination of presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.

Jorge Madrazo Cuellar, who was confirmed by the Mexican Senate on Tuesday a day after President Ernesto Zedillo fired predecessor Antonio Lozano Gracia, said in a series of interviews that the Colosio case would be his top priority.

"I don't believe it's an unsolvable case. But, yes, I do believe it is very tangled, and one of my central tasks will be to untangle it," Madrazo told reporters after being confirmed. "That's my commitment."

Colosio was gunned down at a campaign event in the northern border city of Tijuana. He almost certainly would have become president as candidate of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), in power for 67 straight years.
Zedillo replaced Colosio as candidate and easily won the 1994 election.
Lozano failed spectacularly in his bid to prove the Colosio killing was a wider conspiracy. So far, only one man, confessed shooter Mario Aburto, has been convicted.

Lozano, who as a member of the National Action Party (PAN) was the first opposition party member in a PRI cabinet for decades, also failed to show substantial progress in another high-profile political murder in which the brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari is the prime suspect.
Raul Salinas de Gortari remains in a high-security prison.
Madrazo, a political independent, acknowleded he had "some very delicate affairs" to tend to and some "very urgent actions" to take.

"I think (this job) is like a tiger out of his cage," Madrazo told the TV Azteca television network in an interview. "But I am sure ... we are going to have the legal, vigorous and energetic whip to tame that tiger."
